In this new scattering theory, a quasi-electrostatic image theory is adopted to include the effects of the specular reflection of the incident field and the exact image dipoles induced in the probe tip and the sample substrate. The analytic results from our self-consistent theory are in good agreement with the simulation results obtained by using HFSS, a commercial software based on finite element method.

articleTitle: Analysis of terahertz systems and analytical methods for modeling their optical efficiency
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: This research includes theoretical analysis and experimental testing of terahertz systems operating in the w-band range. In modelling these long wavelength systems we use Gaussian beam mode analysis, a novel technique which can be efficiently used to predict optical behaviour of systems that borrow components from both traditionally established optical and radio receiver techniques. This analytical technique neatly includes diffraction, which dominates propagation in this wavelength range. We are currently investigating the most numerically efficient and stable ways of utilising these modes in optical analysis and present our findings. In parallel, in an experimental campaign, we are characterising standing waves or multiple reflections which occur within terahertz systems. We present the experimental arrangement and outline potential methods to reduce the influence of multiple reflections in terahertz systems.

articleTitle: New test results of 170 GHz/1MW/50%/CW gyrotron for ITER
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The development of 170 GHz/1 MW/ 50%/CW gyrotron for ITER has been in progress in Russia. Recent test results of the last gyrotron version are presented. Stable output power of 0.5-0.6 MW was obtained for 300-s pulse duration limited by capability of the main power supply of that time. For output power of 0.9-0.95 MW the maximal pulse duration of 102 s was mainly limited by instability of gyrotron protection system and imperfection of power transmission line. Total gyrotron efficiency was about 50%. Stray radiation near 5% of radiated power was measured. After testing facility improvement and gyrotron opening and reassembling gyrotron test will be continued.

articleTitle: Development of a high Q open resonator in the 50 GHz to 700 GHz frequency range
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We present the development of a high Q broadband resonator. The symmetric open resonator is designed for the 50 GHz to 700 GHz frequency range using Gaussian Beam Mode theory. Accurate measurements of low loss dielectric materials up to 700 GHz are possible.

articleTitle: THz emission characteristics from LSI-TEG chips under zero bias voltage
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: THz emission characteristics from a large scale integration circuit test element group (LSI-TEG) chip under zero bias condition were investigated to develop the inspection and localization technique of electrical failures in LSI chips without electrical contact, using a laser THz emission microscope (LTEM). The LSI-TEG chip measured in this work contains test circuits composed of p-n junctions and simple metallic line structures such as straight lines with different lengths, bent lines, and interrupted lines. It was found that THz emission waveforms and spectra were strongly influenced by metal line patterns under zero bias condition and its polarizations are parallel to the direction of the line where photocurrent flows. These characteristics are useful for the inspection of LSI chips with electrical failures such as open circuits and short-circuits by comparing the THz emission waveforms and the THz emission images between a normal chip and the tested one, without any electrical contact.

articleTitle: SCUBA-2: A 10000-pixel submillimetre camera for astronomy
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We describe the current status of the SCUBA-2 sub-mm camera for astronomy. We describe the first measurements made while operating an entire sub-array, rather than small subsections as has previously been the case. These results demonstrate that the procedure required to set up the multiplexer for full sub-array operation can be carried out entirely automatically, and that the pixels are sufficiently uniform for the whole sub- array to be usefully operated simultaneously.

articleTitle: Submillimeter-wave schottky diode receivers
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Compact and broadband room temperature receivers are a critical technology for future planetary missions. We report on a room temperature mixer covering the 520 to 600 GHz range with better than 5000 K DSB noise temperature. The receiver front end consists of a bias-able sub-harmonically pumped Schottky mixer and a balanced six anode tripler, both chips made on membrane substrates. This front end in combination with digital backends can provide a low-power, compact, and broadband receiver for future applications.

articleTitle: THz fingerprint spectra detected by sensor chips based on coplanar strip-lines made on low-permittivity plastic substrate
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We have fabricated a coplanar strip-line on low-permittivity Turupica substrate and characterized the terahertz propagation property. The attenuation constant is about 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> at 1.5 THz and is lower than that of the state-of -the-art low-loss coplanar strip-lines with the same pattern on a fused silica substrate. We present a demonstration as a sensor chip working up to as high as 2.5 THz by measuring the finger print spectrum of D-biotin powder.

articleTitle: THz spectroscopy for art conservation science
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The scientific analysis is an important process in art conservation for collecting information of materials used in original work as well as in previous conservation processes. Recently terahertz spectroscopy has progressed rapidly and it is expected that its spectra are more material specific compared with those of mid-infrared regions, so that it can give useful information to identify materials used in art. We have observed spectra of various historical and modern pigments and binders. Almost all pigments in more than 100 specimens have fingerprint peaks, and binders also have specific spectra. Thus, THz spectroscopy can distinguish the pigments which have the same colour, and can distinguish binders used with the same pigment. THz spectroscopy can also identify the transparent body pigment in colour pigments. It should contribute to art conservation as a new non-invasive examination method. Moreover, the firstever THz spectra database of art materials should contribute to the various research fields such as the food and pharmaceutical industries because art materials are also commonly used.

articleTitle: Initial results of AM reflectometory on CPD
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The amplitude modulation reflectometer system has been developed to measure the density profile in detail on the compact PWI (plasma-wall interaction) device (CPD) experiments. The probing frequency range was 6-18 GHz, and its frequency-switching time was 10 mus in an arbitrary step. Using the broadband fast-scanning reflectometer, the wide-range density profile can be measured with high time resolution. In X-mode reflectometory, the developed system successfully measured the phase delay of propagating waves at 6.6, 8.8 and 13.2 GHz, reflected at the vessel wall of the CPD and the R-cutoff layers in the CPD plasma.

articleTitle: Design and performance of the flight configuration SIR on TELIS
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We present the flight configuration and performance of the superconducting integrated receiver (SIR) channel on the TELIS instrument (terahertz and submm limb sounder). The SIR is an on-chip combination of a low-noise SIS mixer with a quasioptical antenna, a superconducting flux flow oscillator (FFO) acting as local oscillator (LO) and an SIS harmonic mixer (HM) for FFO phase locking. The SIR has been assembled, fully integrated into the system and is currently being thoroughly tested in preparation for the flight campaign in October 2007 (Teresina, Brazil).

articleTitle: Continuous wave THz spectrometer based on two LT-GaAs antennas without interdigitated electrodes
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We present an all room-temperature cw THz spectrometer based on robust and low-cost dipole antennas without fragile interdigitated structures. Very accurate spectroscopic measurements and THz image with signal to noise ratio in amplitude exceeding 20 dB are presented. The overall cost, stability and speed of the presented system is superior to the one of the standard THz pulsed spectrometer based on a Ti: Sapphire laser.

articleTitle: Microwave components for 30 GHz high-power gyroklystron
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A 30 GHz high-power gyroklystron is under construction now in IAP (Russia). In the first experiments, carried out at a single pulse regime, RF power 6.5 MW, power gain 30 dB, pulse duration 0.5 mcs, and efficiency 25% were achieved. Next experiments with a new cryogenic magnet and a new electron gun are planned at the second half of 2007 and must demonstrate a repetition rate regime. The gyroklystron has classical three-cavity (TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">52</sub>/TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">52</sub>/TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">53</sub>) scheme and requires a lot of external quasi-optical components: input and output mode converters, a window, and others. It is planned to feed the gyroklystron, using 10 kW magnetron, by means of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> (rectangular) - TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">52</sub> (circular) mode converter connected with the first cavity. The output mode converter is a straight TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">53</sub>- TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">04</sub>-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode transformer with built-in beam collector based on expansion of oversized waveguide. Results of calculations and low power tests of all gyroklystron's components are reported.

articleTitle: Multiline FIR lasers by two wavelength cw CO2 laser pumping
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Simultaneously oscillated multi-line FIR lasers from a single FIR laser cavity pumped by two wavelength CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> lasers have been developed for plasma diagnostics and the other applications. We have obtained simultaneous oscillations as following : (i) 60.5- and 118.8 mum-CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>OH lasers from pumping by 9R(18) CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser and 9P(36) CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser, (ii) 70.5- and 118.8-mum CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>OH lasers from pumping by 9P(34) CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser and 9P(36) CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser, and (iii) 118.8-mum CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>OH and 253.7-mum CD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>OH lasers from pumping by 9P(36) CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser and 10R(36) CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser. An output power of a 118.8-mum CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>OH laser has been enhanced by two same CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser lines pumping.

articleTitle: Progress on design and testing of corrugated waveguide components for ITER ECH&CD transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The performance requirement of 1 (possibly 2) MW cw at 170 GHz for ITER electron cyclotron heating & current drive transmission line components is much more demanding than the 1 MW, 5 to 10 s performance, generally at 110 GHz, that has been demonstrated on present devices. The high ITER heat loads will require enhanced cooling and, for some components, new or modified designs. In addition to thermal management issues, the components must be designed to have very low losses in order to meet the ITER transmission line efficiency requirements. Testing at representative ITER conditions of some components has been initiated at the JAEA 170 GHz gyrotron test stand at Naka, Japan. In addition, testing of a complete prototype ITER transmission line is planned in order to validate the designs for use on ITER. The design changes that are being made for the various components to assure low loss transmission and acceptable component temperatures are presented.

articleTitle: Notice of Retraction: A study of the endogenous electromagnetic field into the space around the flower plants
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Retracted.

articleTitle: Transmittance measurement of human breast tissues in millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Broad-band millimeter wave transmittance measurements of normal and tumorous (cancerous) human breast tissue samples have been acquired in-vitro by employing a free-space, quasi-optical spectrometer. Freshly excised breast tissues were prepared and preserved in 10% neutral-buffered formalin solution before testing. Significant differences in the transmittance profiles have been found between the normal and tumorous tissues. It has been found that despite the inhomogeneity and variable structure and composition of each single tissue, the tumorous specimens consistently manifest much higher absorption level of millimeter wave radiation than the normal ones. It has been shown that free-space, quasi-optical spectrometer is capable of contributing valuable insights into the dielectric properties of normal and tumorous human breast tissues and aiding in further developments of millimeter wave spectroscopy and mammography for breast cancer diagnostics and detection.

articleTitle: A compact CW-THz spectrometer for applications to gas phase identification and quantification of multiple species
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A CW-THz spectrometer using photomixing has been constructed using two external cavity diode lasers and a tapered semiconductor optical amplifier. One diode laser is stabilized to atomic transition of Rubidium and the second is stabilized with a terahertz beatnote separation by means of a low contrast Fabry-Perot interferometer. The line intensity and self broadening coefficient of carbonyl sulphide was determined to validate the spectrometer performance.

articleTitle: Experimental second-harmonic axis-encircling beam gyro-TWT amplifier
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A novel Ka-Band TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> second-harmonic gyro- TWT amplifier with a large-orbit axis-encircling beam from a Northrop Grumman Cusp gun has been fabricated and is being tested at UCD. The device is predicted to produce 50 kW with 20% efficiency, 30 dB saturated gain and 3% bandwidth.

articleTitle: Wavelength calibration for terahertz pulsed spectrometers
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We present methods to deliver traceable frequency measurement for free-space terahertz (THz) radiation disseminated via a stable artefact for 0.3 to 1.5 THz with an uncertainty of 50 GHz.

articleTitle: Computer optimization of electron gun designs
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Computer optimization is applied to three dimensional design of electron guns. The resulting designs exhibit improved performance with significantly reduced design cost compared to manual design. Design tables update geometric parameters in a solid modeling program, including dimensions for points defining spline surfaces. Algorithms then modified the geometry and other parameters based on goal functions defining the desired performance. Optimal designs were achieved by automatic execution of the optimization loop. Results for confined flow Pierce guns, sheet beam guns, and multiple beam guns will be described.

articleTitle: Monitoring the dehydration of collagen by time-domain terahertz transmission measurements
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We measured the change of the terahertz-frequency dielectric properties in collagen hydrated in saline spanning hypo-normal, normal and hyper-normal physiological conditions, during a 24-hour dehydration period in-vitro.

articleTitle: 6.2 Å Sb-based pN diodes for high frequency applications
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Sb-based heterojunction bipolar transistors on semi-insulating GaAs at a = 6.2 Aring consisting of narrow bandgap, p-type In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.27</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.73</sub>Sb and wide bandgap, n-type In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.69</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.31</sub>As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.41</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.59</sub> are demonstrated for the first time. The transistors exhibit excellent current-voltage characteristics. The individual diodes show good forward and reverse operation with saturation current densities and idealities for both the base-emitter and base-collector junctions of 7 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 1.3 and 14 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 1.25, respectively, and a reverse leakage current below 3 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (up to -3 V) for the base-collector junction. Additionally, the transistors display common-emitter current gains up to 20 with common-emitter breakdown voltages of approximately 3 V.

articleTitle: Investigation of electronic states on pressure-tuned heavy electron systems in TmTe by infrared spectromicroscopy under high pressure
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Recent electric resistivity experiments under high pressure have revealed that materials with strongly correlated electrons exhibit under high pressure many interesting and anomalous physical properties such as a new type of pressure-induced metal-insulator transition (for example, electronic phase transition without any lowering of crystal symmetry), generation of unconventional superconductivity, and so on. However, there are very few attempts by optical measurements to study directly the change in the electronic states under high pressure in several GPa range because of the difficulty in experiment in infrared and THz regions. We performed a spectromicroscopic measurement at room temperature in THz to visible region (25 meV−2.5 eV) under high pressure by using a diamond-anvil-cell(DAC). In this paper, we report recent results of the optical study on TmTe which is a typical material of Tm based monochalcogenide compounds. TmTe is a typical divalent semiconductor material with energy band gap of 0.3 eV at ambient conditions but exhibits an interesting electronic phase transition to metallic state via intermediate valent states without any crystal structure change. We found that the pressure-induced metallic state behaves as a heavy electron system.

articleTitle: Coherent synthesis of THz wave profiles
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Coherent synthesis of THz wave spatial profiles was observed using real-time THz imaging. We used an array of photoconductive antennas pumped by femtosecond optical pulses as a THz wave source. Emitted THz pulses were focused and the spatial profile on the focal plane, which is a coherent superposition of output from each unit, was observed by realtime THz imaging using the EO sampling method. By inverting the bias voltage applied to the central unit of the antenna array, a super-resolution effect was observed, where the THz spot sizes was smaller than when a voltage was applied to all the unit in the same direction.

articleTitle: Cyclotron resonance in 2D electron systems of II-VI diluted magnetic semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We have investigated the electron cyclotron resonance in the quantum Hall systems of II–VI semiconductors (Cd1−xMnxTe/CdMgTe quantum well) with the use of the THz and GHz frequency sources at steady high magnetic fields. Anomalous magnetic field dependence of the cyclotron resonance width originating in the localization of carriers has been observed in the CdMnTe/CdMgTe quantum well.

articleTitle: Development of FEM based on coupling of propagating and trapped waves in advanced Bragg resonators
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A novel Bragg FEM scheme [1] is discussed in which an electron beam synchronously interacts with a propagating wave, and the latter is coupled to a quasi cut-off mode. This coupling is realized by either helical or asimuthally symmetric corrugation of the waveguide walls. The quasi cut-off mode provides feedback in the system leading to self-excitation of the whole system while the energy extraction in steady-state regime of generation is almost completely determined by the propagating mode, synchronous to the beam. Analysis based on averaged time domain approach as well as on direct PIC code simulation shows that the efficiency of such a device in the single mode single frequency regime can be rather high. The main advantage of the advanced Bragg resonator is provision of higher selectivity over transverse index than that in the traditional scheme of Bragg FEM. This method can be used for increasing of operating frequency at fixed transverse size of interaction space.The novel feedback scheme should be used on a 8mm FEM based on high current accelerator (0.7 MeV/2 kA/200 ns) at Kanazawa University, Japan.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical components for control of high-power wave flows
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A number of new oversized electrodynamic structures (wave beam dividers/combiners, duplexers, multiplexers, polarizers, etc.) seem promising for long-range communication and radar, microwave technology, particle accelerators and plasma physics at the millimeter wave band.

articleTitle: Plasma scattering measurement in NSTX Tokamak using a submillimeter wave Gyrotron as a radiation source
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Application of high intensity, well-collimated submillimeter probe beam is effective in improving the S/N ratio and the spatial resolution of plasma scattering measurement. High quality operation of the gyrotron and production of well-collimated Gaussian-like beam are required to improve the performance of the measurement. The high quality operation can be achieved by decreasing the fluctuations of the cathode voltage. Gyrotron output is converted into Gaussian-like beam by quasi-optical system consisting of a quasi-optical antenna and focusing mirrors.

articleTitle: Method for synthesis of wideband multimode waveguide units
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Method of waveguide mode converter synthesis was modified to achieve wide frequency band for various elements of microwave transmission lines. Synthesis effectiveness is illustrated by calculated examples of transmission line components. Method allows synthesis of waveguide units with significantly improved characteristics.

articleTitle: The electro magnetic response of human skin in the submillimeter wave range
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The phenomena of non thermal effects of extremely high frequency electromagnetic radiation on biological systems is explored. It is demonstrated that the effect is existent on human beings and is correlated to their physiological state via a measurement of the reflection coefficient of the palm. Possible sources of transient currents in biological systems ,needed to elicit a response are proposed and discussed.

articleTitle: Development of a millimeter and submillimeter wave ESR measurement system
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: In our facility, FIR center Fukui University Japan, several radiation sources of millimeter- and submillimeter-wave are available in addition to high power and high frequency gyrotrons that have been developed successfully. We have developed millimeter and submillimeter wave ESR measurement systems, mainly, to study magnetism at low temperature and in high magnetic field. The ESR measurement systems in our facilities and also recent results of the research of the magnetism are presented.

articleTitle: Low THz absorption of Na3La9B8O27 crystal
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: THz time-domain spectrum of the Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">27</inf>(NLBO) crystal had been measured. The absorption spectrum and other optical constants had been gained through Fourier transform. The absorption coefficient α(ω) is less than 20/cm from 0.1 to 3.0 THz. With the increasing of the frequency, the refractive index n(ω) and the real of dielectric constant ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(ω) steadily and monotonically increase. The n(ω) changes from 3.55 to 3.78, and the ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(ω) changes from 12.7 to 14.2. The imaginary of dielectric constant ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ω) is less than 0.1 from 0.5 to 2.0 THz.

articleTitle: The numerical calculation and analyze of the pulse-laser pumped D2O gas Terahertz laser
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: By using the semi-classical density matrix theory, the pulse-laser pumped D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O gas THz laser was calculated numerically by iteration method and analyzed. According to the result, the THz radiation output spectral characteristic curves were obtained, and the relation between the intensity of pumping laser and the output Tera-Hz laser was studied.

articleTitle: Resistive polarisers and quasi-optical planar isolators
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: In order to construct truly planar quasi-optical isolators it is necessary to develop resistive polarisers, which transmit one linear polarisation and absorb the orthogonal polarisation. We report on two methods of constructing these planar resistive polarisers. The first method uses a "Venetian blind" structure comprising a parallel array of narrow strips of thin absorbing film placed normal to the beam, for which we have demonstrated <0.2 dB insertion loss for E.perpendicular to the absorbing strips and losses up to 40 dB for E.parallel. The return losses at normal incidence were >20 dB for E_parallel and > 30dB for E.perpendicular. The second method uses a resistive wire grid polariser of a specific impedance per square combined with a metallic grid spaced one quarter wavelength away in a configuration similar to a Salisbury screen. These can be built around quarter wavelength matching layers to allow truly planar isolators to be constructed with thicknesses of a few millimetres. Large area planar isolators (325 mm diameter) operating at W-band have achieved 1 dB insertion loss, >20 dB isolation and >17 dB return loss over 75- 90 GHz.

articleTitle: An algorithm for the removal of spurious oscillations from spectra derived from THz time-domain data
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We present a simple algorithm for removing or reducing spurious oscillations in the THz spectra which result from secondary reflection peaks in samples or optical elements. The algorithm utilizes the fact that a THz time-domain trace containing secondary peaks can be represented as a convolution of the main peak and two or more delta functions.

articleTitle: High power THz oulse Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A design for a gyrotron producing radiation from 600 GHz to 2 THz is discussed. The gyrotron is based on a pulse magnet producing a peak field of 37 Tesla, with a 550 microsecond long pulse at a repetition rate of 2.2 Hz. The peak and average powers at 1 THz are 5 kW and 10 W, respectively. The output radiation is in a Gaussian mode.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of GaSe crystal measured by Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the refractive index, absorption coefficient of layered GaSe crystal by means of terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. A unique resonance peak was observed at 0.59 THz (19.6 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> ), which attributes to the E' phonon mode of epsiv-GaSe.

articleTitle: High power THz sources on 4GLS
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Infrared and THz radiation has been available to users of conventional electron accelerator light sources for over a quarter of a century. A new generation of accelerators with sub-picosecond electron bunches provide a massive increase in the power output in the THz region due to coherent enhancement. In this paper, the source properties of the ERLP under construction at Daresbury and the proposed 4GLS sources are discussed. 4GLS will allow multiple beams from THz to soft X-ray to interact with the samples with controlled delay between the ultra short pulses, allowing new scientific possibilities.

articleTitle: Investigation of surface and guided wave polariton modes in doped GaN-AlxGa1−xN multi quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: In this work far infrared attenuated total reflection (ATR) spectroscopy in the Otto configuration has been used to investigate surface phonon-polaritons and guided wave polaritons in doped GaN-Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>N MQW samples. The ATR spectra together with the field profiles and surface polariton dispersion enable the surface modes and guided modes to be identified in the p-polarization spectra.

articleTitle: π-mode formation of hybrid metallic photonic-band-gap coaxial resonator
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: pi-mode formation of hybrid metallic photonic-band-gap (PBG) coaxial resonator for single mode selection is demonstrated by using a finite- difference-time-domain simulation. The TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">911</sub>-mode as a pi-mode in 18-vane hybrid metallic PBG coaxial resonator is filtered by the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub>-mode in the defect area at the resonant frequency of 30.9 GHz.

articleTitle: Development of a compact cherenkov free-electron laser
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A compact Free-Electron Laser operating in the millimeter and terahertz wave range is under development. The radiation is generated via Cherenkov effect of a 50 keV electron beam passing through a waveguide loaded with silicon slabs. Comparing to the conventional undulator based FELs, our device is significantly compact because of the low energy of the electron beam. The size of the device is comparable to the THz sources fed by the solid-state fs lasers. The numerical simulation predicted an output of 2W in average with 1mA/50keV CW electron beam at a frequency of 46 GHz. A test bench using the Spindt cathode as the beam source and a superconducting magnet for the beam focusing was constructed. A preliminary lasing experiment in the millimeter wave range is now under way.

articleTitle: High sensitive detection of biomolecules with integrated THz sensor chip
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We have developed a high sensitive biological sensor chip using a transmission line type terahertz device. The device was based on a transferred low temperature-grown GaAs layer that was bonded onto silicon substrates. Photoconductive switch elements for generating and detecting THz signals are fabricated on the LT-GaAs layer. The sensor chip has a round reservoir on a 1 mm long microstrip transmission line and is able to regulate the interaction length between samples and the THz wave. It can detect the difference between hybridized and denatured DNA molecule with minute volume less than 60 nl (8.4 fmol).

articleTitle: Investigations on an experimental 170 GHz coaxial cavity gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2007 Joint 32nd International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and the 15th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: As part of the European program for development of a 2 MW, CW, 170 GHz coaxial cavity gyrotron, the experimental studies on a short pulse (~ few ms) gyrotron has been continued. A hypothesis concerning the excitation of observed parasitic low frequency (LF) oscillations around 260 MHz has been proven experimentally. Small modifications of the shape of the coaxial insert resulted in an increase of the starting current for the LF oscillations by about a factor of 3 (to above 40 A) causing a strong reduction of the LF amplitude. The influence of the level of microwave stray radiation on gyrotron performance (range of single mode oscillation and efficiency) has been investigated. To improve the performance of the quasi optical (q.o.) RF output system a new launcher with a different wall corrugation and a new adapted phase correcting mirror has been tested both at low power and in the gyrotron. The results are going to be analyzed and compared with simulations.
